facts.text: A hummingbird's wings move in a figure-eight pattern instead of simply flapping up and down.
Hummingbird wings beat dozens of times a second, which lets the birds hover in one place for a long time.
Hummingbirds can fly forward and backward.
Flying, and especially hovering, uses a huge amount of energy, so hummingbirds need sugary food such as flower nectar.
As a hummingbird feeds on nectar, pollen gets on its head and bill and is carried to the next flower, which helps the plant make seeds.
Flowers that hummingbirds visit are often large, red, and shaped like tubes, and they usually have no landing place for insects.
On cold nights, a hummingbird can go into torpor, a deep sleep that saves energy, and it warms up again in the morning.
Hummingbirds live only in the Americas, in North, Central, and South America.
